title: One-Pot Creamy Corn & Potato Soup
description: Potatoes and corn simmer in a lightly creamy broth for a simple inexpensive stovetop soup.
substitutions: Use canned corn, drained, instead of frozen corn.
Use evaporated milk instead of regular milk for a richer soup.
Skip the cheddar for a lighter soup.

steps.text: Add corn and milk, then finish.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 1/2 pounds cubed potatoes, 3 cups broth, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cover and simmer 15–18 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in 2 cups corn and 1 cup milk. Simmer gently 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Mash a few potatoes against the side of the pan to thicken the soup. Stir in 1/2 cup cheddar if using and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently and add a splash of milk or broth if needed.

title: Turkey, Apple & Cheddar Toasties
description: Deli turkey, thin apple slices, and cheddar make a crisp warm sandwich with a sweet-savory crunch.
substitutions: Use deli ham instead of turkey.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Use a thin layer of mayonnaise outside the bread instead of butter.

cookSteps.text: Divide 4 ounces deli turkey, the thin slices from 1 small apple, and 4 slices cheddar between 2 slices bread. Top with the remaining bread and spread 1 tablespoon softened butter over the outsides.
Cook in a large skillet over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until the bread is golden and the cheese is melted.
Rest 1 minute, then cut and serve.

storage: Best served fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat in a dry skillet or toaster oven.

title: Leftover Vegetable & Egg Noodle Skillet
description: Cooked vegetables and egg noodles get a quick buttery skillet refresh instead of another plain reheated side.
substitutions: Use cooked spaghetti or other leftover pasta instead of egg noodles.
Use any mixture of cooked broccoli, carrots, peas, cabbage, zucchini, or green beans.
Use shredded cheddar instead of Parmesan.

cookSteps.text: Melt 2 tablespoons butter or heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 2 cups chopped leftover cooked vegetables and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder; cook 3 minutes.
Add 3 cups cooked egg noodles and cook 5–7 minutes, tossing often, until everything is steaming hot and a few noodle edges are lightly golden.
Stir in 1/4 cup Parmesan if using and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Cinnamon Raisin Bread Pudding
description: A few cups of stale bread become a soft cinnamon custard dessert with raisins and ordinary pantry staples.
substitutions: Use chopped apple instead of raisins.
Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Use brioche, sandwich bread, or leftover rolls.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a small baking dish. Put 4 cups stale bread cubes and 1/2 cup raisins in the dish.
Whisk 2 eggs, 1 1/4 cups milk, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using. Pour over the bread and press gently so the cubes absorb the custard. Rest 5 minutes.
Bake 28–30 minutes, until the center is set and the top is lightly browned.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Serve chilled or reheat individual portions gently.
